# Rome 46 BC – Life sciences

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Microorganisms (living things too small to see)** [`microorganisms`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/microorganisms.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept medium. Varro's invisible marsh animals are a guess, not an observation. No lenses: glass is cast, coloured and bubbly. A tiny clear bead of glass or rock crystal is the route. Local: Marcus Terentius Varro; gem engravers working rock crystal.
- **Life comes only from life (spontaneous generation refuted)** [`spontaneous_generation_refuted`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/spontaneous_generation_refuted.md) — K0, use wrong, make easy, accept medium. Aristotle and every farmer: maggots from rotting meat, eels from mud, bees from an ox carcass (in Mago's farming book too). The covered-jar experiment is cheap.
- **Fermentation is the work of living yeast** [`fermentation_yeast`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fermentation_yeast.md) — K0, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Must ferments by itself in the dolium; bread rises with kept leaven. It is called a boiling (fervere). Showing that yeast is alive needs a microscope.
- **Cell theory** [`cell_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cell_theory.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low
- **Viruses (disease agents smaller than bacteria)** [`viruses`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/viruses.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept low
- **Systematic classification and naming of living things** [`taxonomy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/taxonomy.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Aristotle's animal books and Theophrastus' plant books exist in Greek, as does Crateuas' illustrated herbal. Romans name plants by use. No fixed species names or ranks. Local: Greek libraries of Roman nobles (that of the Luculli at Tusculum). Elsewhere: Athens and Alexandria, Peripatetic natural history.
- **Egg, sperm and fertilisation** [`reproduction_fertilisation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reproduction_fertilisation.md) — K1, use wrong, make hard, accept low. Two rival theories: Aristotle's (male seed gives form, female only matter) and the Hippocratic and Epicurean two-seed view. Egg and sperm cannot be shown without a microscope.
- **Heredity by discrete factors (Mendel)** [`heredity_genetics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/heredity_genetics.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept medium. Likeness to parents and grandparents is noticed (Lucretius book 4) and explained by mixed seed. Counting pea crosses takes several seasons and a patient villa owner.
- **Evolution by natural selection** [`evolution_natural_selection`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/evolution_natural_selection.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Lucretius (book 5) has earth produce many creatures of which the unfit died out, but species do not change. Epicureans may listen; Stoics see design and providence. Local: Lucretius, De rerum natura, book 5; Epicurean circles in Rome and at Herculaneum.
- **DNA is the hereditary material (double helix)** [`dna_structure`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/dna_structure.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept low
- **Breathing is slow combustion (respiration and body heat)** [`respiration_metabolism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/respiration_metabolism.md) — K0, use wrong, make hard, accept low. Breath cools the innate heat of the heart (Aristotle) or supplies pneuma to the arteries (Erasistratus). A mouse and a lamp under a jar is a demonstration anyone can see.
- **Plants are built from air, water and light (photosynthesis and mineral nutrition)** [`photosynthesis_plant_nutrition`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/photosynthesis_plant_nutrition.md) — K0, use wrong, make hard, accept low. Plants eat soil through their roots (Aristotle), so soil 'tires'. The weighed-pot willow experiment is easy and takes years; the gas part needs chemistry that is absent.
- **Legumes fix nitrogen from the air (root nodule bacteria)** [`nitrogen_fixation_biology`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/nitrogen_fixation_biology.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Farmers know that lupins, beans and vetch 'dung the land' (Cato 37) and plough them in. Why is unknown; nodules on the roots are visible to anyone who looks. Local: Cato, De agri cultura; Mago's farming books in Latin and Greek.
- **The brain and nerves (seat of thought, electrical signalling)** [`nervous_system_brain`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/nervous_system_brain.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. Herophilus and Erasistratus traced nerves to the brain, and physicians follow them. Aristotelians, Stoics and Epicureans (Lucretius) keep the mind in the chest. Electrical signalling is unreachable. Elsewhere: Alexandria, anatomical books of Herophilus and Erasistratus.
